plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because winning requires bidding higher than others, but paying the second-highest bid means overbidding significantly reduces profit. Since this is round 1, and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value to attempt a win while minimizing payment. I will bid $12.6.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value is $10. However, my value is $25. To maximize profit, I should bid a small increment above what I expect the others to bid, while still being below my value. I'll bid $10.10.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and the auction rules (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid), the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value. However, since values are capped at $20, and mine is $29, I must bid the maximum allowed, $20. This ensures I win if any other bidder's value is less than $20.
